name: Khayyam
comment: Display roles are specified in modules/khayyam/display/display.json and explained in modules/khayyam/display/display.md; that contract is authoritative and governs how Khayyam is displayed to any reader, not only in an editor. Each rule below names the roles it serves in its `comment`. Rules are ordered so the most specific form of a line wins: an inclusion, then a declaration that opens a block, then a method declaration that carries its signature, then the generic rules.

inclusion.comment: Roles: keyword, included-type, included-variable, subtype, file-uri. Type Inclusion and Variable Inclusion (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Import Mechanism).

capsule-declaration.comment: Roles: keyword, subtype, capsule, capsule-field, type-reference. A capsule is `tp {name} cp { ... }`; its body is field lines `fieldName fieldType` plus one-token lines that are bare abstraction names, which are type references (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Capsule; docs/khayyam/encapsulation.md, Capsule Structure and Privacy). The second rule is the same declaration without a block, so the name keeps its role while the block is still being typed.

patterns.comment: Role: capsule-field. A name followed by another name on the line is a field.
Role: type-reference. The field's type, or a bare abstraction name on its own line.

abstraction-declaration.comment: Roles: keyword, subtype, abstraction, type-reference. An abstraction is `tp {name} ab { ... }` and every line in its block is a bare abstraction name, so every identifier there is a type reference. The block is optional in the language, so the second rule carries the same roles for the bodiless form.

method-declaration.comment: Roles: keyword, subtype, method, method-owner-type, method-argument, method-argument-type. The three parenthesised groups are the owner, the influencing and the influenced variables (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Method). Groups 5-12 are the influencing group and 13-20 the influenced group, alternating argument name and argument type, four pairs each. A fifth pair in a group is left uncaptured, and its names take the identifier-reference role; the largest group in the corpus holds three pairs.

scope-declaration.comment: Roles: keyword, subtype, scope. A code scope is `tp {name} sc { ... }` (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Scope).

variable-declaration.comment: Roles: keyword, variable, type-reference. `vr {name} {type}` (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Variable). The name takes `variable`, which is the role for a declaration at FILE LEVEL. A `vr` standing inside a method body is `method-local`, and this rule cannot tell the two apart: it matches one line at a time, and the line that opened the body is not on the line the `vr` stands on. The contract therefore declares `method-local` server-only, and this rule's claim at a body's `vr` is a position claim rather than a resolved one - the language server answers the same characters with `method-local`, and the editor's merge gives the server's answer precedence wherever the server answers.

method-call.comment: Role: method. The dot operator is the language's only invocation form, so the name before the opening parenthesis at a call site is a Method and carries the same role as its declaration (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Method Invocation Rules).

subtype-keywords.comment: Role: subtype. The five subtype keywords wherever they appear without a declaration to attach to.
subtype-keywords.name: keyword.control.subtype.khayyam

keywords.comment: Role: keyword. `tp` and `vr` are reserved words (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Language Keyword in a Glance).
keywords.name: keyword.control.khayyam

strings.comment: Role: string. The language has no string literal, so this rule has no form to match today; it exists so a quoted form has no unstyled fallback if one is added.
strings.name: string.quoted.double.khayyam

illegal-numbers.comment: Role: invalid-number. A bare number is not a value the language admits (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, No primitive types).
illegal-numbers.name: invalid.illegal.numeric.khayyam

illegal-operators.comment: Role: invalid-operator. The grammar admits no operator character; the dot of invocation is the only one.
illegal-operators.name: invalid.illegal.operator.khayyam

identifiers.comment: Role: identifier-reference. An identifier begins with a letter or '_', then letters, digits or '_', in any script (docs/khayyam/khayyam.md, Identifiers). A bare identifier here is a use whose binding this profile cannot state, so it must not read as a local declaration.
identifiers.name: variable.other.reference.khayyam
